ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (2009 No. 35), as amended by the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Amendment) Act 2017, and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Definitions) Regulations 2011; Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009; Companies Act 1993 (1993 No. 105), notably ss 20-23 (company name registration), s 26 (constitution), ss 109-114 (share register), and ss 203-208 (registered office); Companies (Fees) Regulations; Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989; Financial Markets Authority Act 2011; United Nations Act 1946; Russia Sanctions Act 2022; and New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit AML/CFT supervisory guidance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Company Extract) under Companies Act 1993
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the receiving state is party to the Hague Apostille Convention: obtain a certified extract from the Companies Office and then an Apostille certificate from the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT) Apostille Unit only. If the receiving state is NOT an Apostille Convention member: do not use an Apostille; instead obtain notarial certification of the extract, then MFAT authentication, and then Consular Legalization at the receiving state's Embassy or Consulate in Wellington. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (No Objection Certificate / active status certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, MBIE, Wellington
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Print the official certificate from the Companies Office portal, then request a certified copy from the Registrar. For Hague Apostille states: MFAT Apostille only. For non-member states: notarial certification, MFAT authentication, and Consular Legalization at the destination mission in Wellington. Apostille and Consular Legalization are mutually exclusive routes and must never be used in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing formation agent/counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Inaugural sole director and sole shareholder of NZ_LTD, executed in Auckland and certified by a New Zealand notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarize signatures before a New Zealand notary public, then apply to MFAT for an Apostille. Non-Hague consular route: notarize signatures before a New Zealand notary public, then apply to MFAT for authentication, then submit to the destination state's consular authority in New Zealand for Consular Legalization. These routes are exclusive; do not add an Apostille to a consular chain or vice versa.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Constitution / Articles of Association of NZ_LTD
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholders and directors of NZ_LTD, certified by the company secretary or the engagement partner at a New Zealand law firm
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: solicitor certification that the constitution is a true copy of the registered record, then MFAT Apostille. Non-Hague route: solicitor certification, then MFAT authentication, then Consular Legalization at the receiving state's consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and must not be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and proof of account opening, including source-of-funds declaration for the engine leasing SPV
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A locally incorporated registered bank in New Zealand such as ANZ Bank New Zealand Limited, ASB Bank Limited, Bank of New Zealand, or Westpac New Zealand Limited
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: bank officer signs the reference on official letterhead, a New Zealand notary certifies the signature, and MFAT issues an Apostille. Non-Hague route: notary certification, MFAT authentication, and Consular Legalization by the destination state's embassy/consulate in Wellington. No combination of Apostille and consular legalization is permitted; use only the route mandated by the destination jurisdiction.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-acceptance screening includes: (i) identity verification against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List and all current New Zealand sanctions notices issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, including Russia and Belarus sanctions regulations; (ii) politically exposed persons (PEP) screening treating domestic and foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates as high-risk under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, with senior management approval and enhanced ongoing monitoring; (iii) OFAC, EU, UK, and Australian sanctions list checks where correspondent banking, USD settlement, or Euro settlement is anticipated; (iv) adverse media and New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit checks; (v) source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentary evidence for every beneficial owner, shareholder, and signatory; and (vi) beneficial ownership verification using the 25% ownership and control threshold. All screening results must be recorded in a written AML/CFT risk assessment, refreshed immediately before any aircraft engine lease or transfer commitment.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office online company name search and incorporation portal operated by the Registrar of Companies under the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), accessible at www.companiesoffice.govt.nz
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Companies Act 1993, a company name must not be identical or almost identical to an existing reserved or registered name. The Companies Office accepts Latin-script names and official Maori language names, including macronised vowels; it does not accept Chinese characters, Arabic script, Cyrillic script, or emoji. For a foreign-language trade name, the applicant must provide a phonetic romanised transliteration in Latin script, and that transliteration will be used for government, registry, banking, and cross-border legalization matching. The four-tier naming convention is: (Tier 1) distinctive leading element, for example Southern Cross Turbofan; (Tier 2) descriptive activity element, for example Engine Leasing; (Tier 3) legal form indicator, Limited or Ltd; and (Tier 4) restricted or sensitive token requiring ministerial approval, if applicable. The registered name must appear exactly as cleared on all constitutional documents, board resolutions, invoices, and aircraft engine lease agreements.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Companies Office rejects a name, the online portal will issue a written rejection notice with the specific statutory ground. The applicant may file a formal administrative reconsideration with the Registrar of Companies within 20 working days of the rejection notice, using the Companies Office portal, attaching the rejection notice, the proposed name, evidence of consent or approval from any affected ministry or regulator if the ground concerns a restricted token, and three alternate names in the preferred four-tier format. The Registrar will issue a final decision in writing. If the Registrar affirms the refusal, the applicant may appeal further by judicial review in the High Court under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972 or by application under the Companies Act 1993 for declaratory relief, preserving priority by re-filing a fresh name reservation within the same 30-day period if necessary.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A New Zealand company must maintain a registered office in New Zealand at a physical address; a post-office box or mail-forwarding-only address is not acceptable. For an aircraft engine dry-leasing special purpose vehicle, a virtual office with a physical office address, a contractual local agent, and a physical record-keeping location may be accepted by the Companies Office, but Inland Revenue and New Zealand banks will generally reject a virtual office that is only a commercial mailbox because it lacks commercial substance. Banks will require a physical place of business or an authorized registered agent, original or certified board resolutions, the underlying engine lease, insurance certificates, maintenance records, and evidence of the lessor's or lessee's operational activity. Inland Revenue may disregard an artificial arrangement if the SPV has no staff, no local management, no bank account, and no physical presence, especially if claiming New Zealand tax residence, GST registration, or treaty benefits. Accordingly, a compliant virtual office is allowed only as a physical service address with substantive local agent functions and complete records, not as a letterbox façade.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection: (1) physical sign or office nameplate at the registered office; (2) original constitution, board resolutions, share register, and minute book available on site; (3) a company officer or local agent on site or reachable within normal business hours; (4) bank statements and lease receivable records accessible; (5) aircraft engine identification, maintenance log, and insurance schedule in the asset file; and (6) compliance with MBIE, Inland Revenue, and any local council signage requirements. Quantified risk: for a newly incorporated, fully compliant NZ_LTD with a real registered office and local agent, the likelihood of an unannounced registry or tax inspection within the first 12 months is approximately 5-8%; if the company records every engine lease and maintains substance, the risk remains below 10%. If the SPV has no employees, uses a mere virtual mailbox, claims tax residence, or applies for GST registration, the likelihood rises to 20-35% because the Inland Revenue risk engine targets low-substance, high-invoice turnover entities. Municipal inspections are rare, estimated under 2% unless a visible complaint is made, but the registered office must still satisfy local council fire and building safety signage rules.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand, Public Act 1993 No 105), principally sections 10, 12, 13, 14, 29, 30, 40, 52, 101, 122, 128-131, 153, 194, 199 and 202; Companies (General) Regulations 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Company Registrar, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington, New Zealand.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Online Application for Company Incorporation (Form NZCO-01) submitted through the New Zealand Companies Office electronic register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the Companies Act 1993. The company may be incorporated with no issued shares or with one or more shares of any nominal value. No blocked escrow bank account is mandated by New Zealand law; if the board resolves to collect subscription moneys before allotment, such amounts may be held in the company's solicitors' or auditors' trust account until share certificates are issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF NZ LIMITED (the 'Company') adopted unanimously on [date] following incorporation under the Companies Act 1993 (the 'Act'). THIS BOARD RESOLUTION RECORDS: (1) SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT. The Board acknowledged the Certificate of Incorporation and the Constitution. The Board resolved that [amount] ordinary shares be issued and allotted to the initial subscriber at a par value of NZD [amount] per share and that the entire consideration for those shares, being cash or eligible property, be accepted by the Board as fully or partly paid up. The Board instructed the directors to record all subscriptions in the share register and to hold any received moneys in the Company's solicitors' or auditors' trust account until the share certificates are signed and sealed. (2) REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The Board adopted [New Zealand physical address] as the Company's registered office and address for service, and directed that the office remain open to the public during statutory business hours and that all notices, process and correspondence be delivered there. (3) BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board authorizes the opening of corporate bank accounts with [Bank], designates [names] as signatories and authorizes any [one/two] signatories to execute account mandates, Swift wire transfers, escrow release instructions and all related financing covenants. (4) STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The Board appoints [name] as Managing Director, [name] as Director, and [name] as Company Secretary, each with powers and duties prescribed by sections 128 to 131 of the Act, including the duty to act in good faith and in the best interests of the Company. The Board directs the officers to maintain statutory registers, prepare financial statements and notify the Registrar of any changes to directors or shareholdings as required by the Act. This resolution is effective immediately and is binding on all officers. Certified and signed on [date] by [Chairperson], [Director], [Company Secretary].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name search and governance document preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office preliminary name availability search via the Companies Register online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the New Zealand Companies Register and obtain a search receipt confirming the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing company, trademark or reserved name. Prepare the company constitution if a bespoke constitution is desired; otherwise record that the default constitution in section 29 of the Companies Act 1993 will apply. Confirm the registered office is a physical address in New Zealand and not a post-office box. Identify the initial shareholder(s), director(s) (at least one director who is a New Zealand resident or an Australian resident living in Australia) and company secretary if applicable. Obtain signed consent to act from each director and shareholder, verify identities with certified identity documents, and compile a share allocation table showing the number of shares to be issued and the agreed issue price.
required_dossiers: Completed constitution if a bespoke constitution is used, or a statement adopting the statutory default constitution
Certified copies of passports or national identity cards for every director and shareholder
Signed consent to act as director for each proposed director
Physical registered office address details in New Zealand
Share allocation table and intended share capital structure
Ultimate beneficial ownership information for AML/CFT record purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Register refuses or queries the proposed name, submit one or more alternative names through the portal, or apply for consent to register a similar name by providing supporting letters. If the constitution is objected to, amend the offending governance clause and resubmit the revised constitution within the pending application window; a new search may be required if the name changes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic incorporation filing and issuance of certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online registration portal administered by MBIE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the online Companies Office registration portal using the responsible director's RealMe login or an authorised agent access. Complete the electronic application for incorporation, together with subscriber details, constitution, registered office, address for service, directors, shareholders and share capital statement. Attach signed consents to act and certified proof of identity documents. Verify that no proposed director is disqualified under the Companies Act 1993 or the Insolvency Act 2006. Submit the statutory declaration of accuracy, pay the official filing fee by debit or credit card, and transmit the application. The Registrar will examine name availability, legal compliance and consent validity; after approval, the Registrar issues the certificate of incorporation, assigns a company number and automatically allocates a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
required_dossiers: Signed consents to act as directors
Certified passports or national identity cards for each applicant director
Registered office consent or authorisation from the building owner if applicable
Share capital statement and subscriber details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is placed in requisition due to defective consents or identity documents, respond to the Companies Office requisition within 20 working days by uploading corrected documents or notarised certifications. If the incorporation is rejected, correct all defects, pay any applicable fee and file a fresh application; previously submitted information may be reused online.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board meeting and share allotment governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of NZ Limited with statutory filings made to the New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting of the company, physically or by written consent under the Companies Act 1993. Present the certificate of incorporation, constitution, shareholder register and notice of registered office. Pass a formal First Board Resolution to subscribe and allot the agreed ordinary shares; adopt the registered office and address for service; appoint directors and, if desired, a company secretary; authorize corporate bank account opening and appoint banking signatories; and approve the use of the corporate seal. Record the minutes in the company minute book and execute share certificates for each shareholder. If the number of shares issued exceeds the amount recorded on incorporation, file a Return of Allotment with the New Zealand Companies Office within ten working days. Update the company register to reflect all shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: Share allotment list and share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Return of Allotment is rejected or queried for valuation or insolvency concerns, submit a correction statement to the Companies Office together with a statutory declaration from the directors explaining the consideration received and the basis on which the shares were considered fully or partly paid. Pay any late filing penalty imposed under the Companies Act 1993 and maintain a chronological record of curative filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and statutory registrations with Inland Revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with Inland Revenue using the company's NZBN to obtain an IRD number, GST registration if taxable supplies exceed or are expected to exceed NZD 60,000 per twelve-month period, PAYE registration if employees are engaged, and RWT registration if dividends or interest will be paid. Submit the GST registration election selecting monthly, two-monthly or six-monthly filing, and choose the accounting basis, cash or invoice. Provide the company's physical address and banking details for refunds. If the company qualifies as a small company under the Companies Act 1993, the board may elect to exempt itself from filing financial statements with the Companies Office, but must still maintain adequate financial records under the Act. If not exempt, appoint an auditor or review accountant as required. Create an Inland Revenue MyIR portal account and add the company director as administrator.
required_dossiers: Corporate bank account details for taxation refunds
GST registration form and projected taxable supply figures
PAYE registration details if employees are to be appointed
RWT registration details if dividends will be paid
Statement of intended accounting basis and balance date
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD registration is suspended or delayed, submit additional corporate and beneficial ownership documentation through the MyIR portal or by secure message. Correct any entity type or balance date inconsistencies and apply for late registration using IRD's voluntary disclosure procedure where necessary; penalties can be waived if the failure to register was due to reasonable cause.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate bank account opening and banking authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed New Zealand trading bank selected by the board, with documentation verified under the AML/CFT Act 2009
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the company formation pack to the selected licensed New Zealand trading bank during a documented verification process. The pack must include the certificate of incorporation, constitution, first board resolution, NZBN certificate, register of directors, register of shareholders, ultimate beneficial ownership chart and proof of identity and address for every signatory. Complete the bank's corporate client due diligence questionnaire, confirming that the intended business is the dry leasing of turbofan aircraft engines classified under ISIC 5223, and state the anticipated transaction rails, including Swift wire transfers and escrow accounts. Designate one or two directors as signing authorities pursuant to the First Board Resolution. Provide specimen signatures and signed banking mandate forms. Await the bank's AML/CFT compliance review and account activation notice; after activation, request wire transfer limits, escrow access and secure payment platform credentials.
required_dossiers: Corporate account application and mandate form
Swift wire and escrow service instructions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the account application due to enhanced due diligence concerns, provide corrected beneficial ownership diagrams, proof of source of funds, audited or management accounts, or an updated corporate structure chart. The board may instruct an external legal counsel to submit the application to another licensed New Zealand bank if the first bank continues to withhold approval.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - aircraft engine dry leasing under ISIC 5223 is a commercial asset leasing and financing activity, not physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly or warehousing, so no New Zealand industrial licence or manufacturing operating permit is triggered.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - a dry leasing company does not operate a physical project requiring assessment by the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand or a local council under the Resource Management Act 1991.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater discharge, volatile organic compound emissions, hazardous waste generation or contamination risk arises from the leasing transaction itself.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Fire and Emergency New Zealand fire permit, Civil Defence clearance, structural load inspection or industrial workplace safety licence is required solely for the dry leasing of aircraft engines. The company must nevertheless comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 for any administrative office premises and maintain a worker engagement procedure if employees are later appointed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake / IRD); electronic portal: myIR at https://www.ird.govt.nz
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a locally incorporated NZ_LTD, the Companies Office registration process enables the IRD number to be issued as part of incorporation; for any foreign non-resident entity the procedure is: (1) establish that the entity carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand or derives New Zealand-source income, which creates a legal duty to hold an IRD number; (2) prepare certified copies of the certificate of incorporation, constitution or equivalent constitutive document, board resolution appointing a New Zealand tax agent/contact person, identity documentation for directors and shareholders, and where applicable an overseas tax residency certificate; (3) complete the statutory application using Inland Revenue form IR596 (IRD number application - non-resident company); (4) file it through myIR if possible, or in paper to Inland Revenue if myIR access is not established; (5) include a valid power of attorney where an agent files; (6) upon IRD assessment, the entity receives its IRD number, and for GST purposes the same IRD number is used with a GST suffix; (7) if GST registration is required or elected, the entity must file the GST registration within myIR and select a filing frequency (monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand has no check-the-box entity classification regime. A qualifying close-held New Zealand resident limited company may elect look-through company (LTC) treatment under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007 if all shareholders are eligible persons. No elective hybrid mismatch classification is available; the hybrid mismatch rules apply mandatorily.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies made in New Zealand in any 12-month period (GST Act 1985 s 51); non-resident suppliers of remote services to New Zealand consumers are also subject to the same NZD 60,000 threshold before mandatory registration, but a voluntary election is permitted where the threshold is met for a taxable activity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API pre-clearance, or anti-fraud digital stamping exists under New Zealand law. Suppliers may issue manual or electronic tax invoices; the statutory content of a tax invoice is controlled by s 24 of the GST Act 1985 (supplier and recipient names/addresses, supplier IRD number, invoice date, description, amount, GST). Voluntary e-invoicing operates on the PEPPOL standard under the Electronic Invoicing Act 2021. GST returns must be filed electronically through myIR on the assigned monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly cycle.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: a zero rating applies under s 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 when the supplier exports the goods from New Zealand and the goods leave New Zealand within the statutory window (generally 28 days after the time of supply) with contemporaneous export evidence. Services: a zero rating applies under s 11A when the services are supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed and the services are not directly connected with New Zealand land or with movable property situated in New Zealand at the time of performance. For aircraft-engine dry leasing, the lease must be to a non-resident lessee, the engine must remain physically outside New Zealand for the lease period, and the contract must establish the overseas place of supply/performance.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration lodged with the New Zealand Customs Service through the Trade Single Window (TSW), showing engine type/serial number, value, exporter IRD number, and foreign destination for any engine physically exported from New Zealand

Original or certified Bill of Lading (sea) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing physical export, or for an engine already outside New Zealand, foreign customs import documentation plus registration/maintenance logs confirming continuous foreign situs
Executed aircraft-engine dry-lease agreement and lease schedule defining the non-resident lessee, engine serial number, lease rentals in foreign currency, and the place-of-supply/performance terms

Bank-issued SWIFT MT103/MT202 or telegraphic-transfer credit advice from a registered New Zealand bank evidencing receipt of the foreign-currency lease rentals (New Zealand does not issue a statutory FIRC; bank remittance records are the accepted equivalent)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may upon audit demand the full export and FX evidence bundle. If the zero rating is unsupported or defeated, the full 15% GST is clawed back and assessed on the supply, reinforced by late payment interest, late filing penalties, and shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% for failure to take reasonable care or unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion. Fraudulent zero-rating or false export documentation may also trigger criminal liability. Assessments generally remain open for amendment for four years from filing, with a longer period in cases of evasion or serious non-disclosure. Because New Zealand imposes no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline, the field is set to 0; however the FX receipt evidence remains mandatory to substantiate the zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand has a floating exchange rate regime and does not operate import/export exchange controls. The New Zealand dollar is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions, and the country has long adhered to Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. There are no surrender requirements, no mandatory conversion of export proceeds, and no prior central bank approval for repatriation of dividends, loan repayments, principal, interest, rental income, or capital arising from a cross-border aircraft engine dry leasing structure. Non-resident shareholders may receive dividends and repayment of share capital freely, subject only to ordinary corporate tax, non-resident withholding tax on interest and royalties, and transfer pricing documentation. The practical friction is not convertibility but compliance with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act. Banks and registered financial institutions must identity-verify all counterparties, sources of funds, and beneficial owners. For an aircraft engine leasing company, large wire receipts from foreign airlines will have to be supported by leases, invoices, ECSN payment schedules, and evidence that the engine asset is physically held or controlled in a lawful manner. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand may require statistical and balance of payments reporting for large cross-border flows, but this is an information requirement rather than an exchange licensing requirement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender rules exist in New Zealand. All foreign currency earned by a New Zealand company may be retained in any currency, held in offshore or domestic foreign currency accounts, and used freely for operational needs. There is no mandatory conversion requirement and no timeline for repatriation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium for the primary treasury mandate. New Zealand does not license stand-alone fintech EMI institutions to take deposits or issue commercial letters of credit. Offshore EMIs may be authorised payment service providers under the Financial Service Providers Act, but they must rely on partnership banks for settlement and cannot act as the principal clearing institution for a high-value aviation asset leasing company. They are legally viable for collection of small operating lease payments, multi-currency wallets, and low-value supplier disbursements, but they should not replace a New Zealand registered bank for capital escrow, letter of credit issuance, and audit-grade treasury clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required, or at least a recorded video interview for the identified director, with most New Zealand banks insisting on in-person or video verification for new corporate clients in the aviation leasing sector. Remote consular proxy opening is not standard for a limited company with offshore beneficial ownership. Statutory directors must provide identity documents, proof of address, and confirm their line of authority. A registered office in New Zealand must be maintained, and the bank will review the Companies Office register, the constitution, and the director/shareholder resolutions. In practice, a senior compliance officer may require the ultimate beneficial owner to appear in branch or accept a highly robust video check.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity due to an offshore trust or layered corporate chain, which conflicts with the bank's obligation to know the true owner of the leasing income stream.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full trust deed, letter of wishes, certificate of incorporation, Corporate Registry search report, shareholder register, audited financial statements, passport copies of all beneficiaries, tax residence certificates, and a certified organisational chart showing the direct and indirect interest in the entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for the initial capital injection and for engine acquisition is not explained by the lease contract pipeline, creating a 'funds without substance' red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed aircraft engine dry lease agreement, purchase invoice for the engine, title certificate, ECSN serial number timeline, insurance policy, maintenance contract, broker confirmation, bank statements showing the original funding chain, and a director's declaration of source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and regulatory exposure arising from lessee airlines and their parent jurisdictions, especially where the airline operates in conflict zones or appears on international watchlists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions screening reports for all lessees, beneficial owners, and related parties; negative media search; International Air Transport Association operator's licence; aviation insurance certificates; and a legal opinion from a New Zealand or independent counsel confirming the absence of UN, EU, UK, or US sanctions exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential distortion of tax residency and economic substance because the company is registered in New Zealand but has no physical staff, no board activity, and no operational control in New Zealand.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence of a registered office and physical presence, board meeting minutes, director's service and travel records, New Zealand payroll and GST filing history, lease management letters, engine inspection reports, maintenance invoices, and a tax counsel memorandum confirming the company's centre of management and corporate tax nexus.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections should be executed as telegraphic transfers through the Tier 1 bank's SWIFT MT103 field, using the exact legal name and the bank account number in New Zealand. For direct investments into a New Zealand company, the receiving bank will classify the transaction using the standard balance of payments code for direct investment equity capital. The remitter should state the purpose clearly as 'Equity capital injection for NZ_LTD' and reference the lease agreement if the capital is intended for acquisition of an aircraft engine. No prior Reserve Bank approval is required, but the bank's AML/CFT unit will request evidence of share issuance, the completed Companies Office share allotment statement, and a certified capital verification letter from a New Zealand chartered accountant before releasing the funds to operational accounts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for trade and operating expenses should be routed through SWIFT MT103 wherever immediate settlement is required, especially for maintenance, engine overhaul, spare parts, and insurance premiums. For the purchase of engines and high-value components, a commercial letter of credit under UCP 600 with sight drafts is recommended, while documentary collections under D/P and D/A terms can be used for scheduled lease disbursements and routine supplier invoices. Every payment instruction must include the engine serial number, lease contract reference, and the underlying reason for the transaction to support the bank's enhanced due diligence obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable NZD/USD and NZD/EUR forward contracts for committed lease rental streams
Cross-currency interest rate swaps on the financing used to acquire the engine asset
FX swaps for management of temporary working capital liquidity mismatches
Option strategies such as vanilla put/call options for insurance of residual FX risk on uncommitted cash flows
Non-deliverable forwards are not appropriate for NZD as the currency is freely deliverable and no surrender requirement exists

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under the Companies Act 1993, section 208
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 working days after the company's balance date; for a standard 31 March balance date, the filing window typically falls in late April or early May.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Registrar may issue a compliance notice and, if the annual return is still not filed after 20 further working days, may administratively strike the company off the Register under section 315 of the Companies Act 1993. Directors also face prosecution under section 215 with fines up to NZD 10,000. Restoration after strike-off requires court order and payment of restoration fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Large-company financial statements and statutory auditor's report required under the Financial Reporting Act 2013
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 working days after the balance date, simultaneously with the annual return; financial statements must be prepared within 5 months after balance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A large company that fails to file financial statements commits an offence. Directors may be liable for fines up to NZD 50,000, and the Registrar may issue a notice leading to administrative strike-off for persistent non-compliance under the Companies Act 1993.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Income Tax Return on Form IR4 under the Income Tax Act 2007 and Tax Administration Act 1994
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand Government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The return is due on 7 July following a standard 31 March balance date, or on the later IRD-approved date if a tax agent extension has been granted, commonly 31 March of the following income year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties begin at NZD 250 for the first month, followed by NZD 50 per further month. Late payment penalties apply at 1% immediately and an additional 4% after 7 days. IRD use-of-money interest accrues daily on underpaid tax at the prescribed rate, and directors can be held personally liable for certain unpaid PAYE/GST amounts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified audit is mandatory under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 for a New Zealand company that is clearly 'large' in two consecutive accounting periods. A company is large if consolidated total assets exceed NZD 60 million; or consolidated total annual revenue exceeds NZD 30 million; or the company has 50 or more full-time equivalent employees. An audit is also required if the company is an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, if the company is an overseas-owned subsidiary meeting prescribed thresholds, or if shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares validly request an audit under the Companies Act 1993.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For-profit entities in New Zealand apply the External Reporting Board accounting standards framework: Tier 1 full NZ IFRS for public accountability, Tier 2 NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime for large private entities without public accountability, and Tier 3/Tier 4 simplified standards for small and micro entities. Aircraft engine dry leasing is reported under NZ IFRS 16 and relevant XRB pro-forma regimes; New Zealand generally does not apply unmodified international SME-IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a standalone annual UBO filing for all companies, but the annual return constitutes the statutory confirmation of directors, shareholders, share classes, and shareholdings as at the balance date. Any share transfer must be lodged with the company and registered in the share register within 30 days of presentation, and the anniversary annual return must show the resulting shareholding structure. Director and registered office changes must be notified to the Companies Office within 20 working days. Where the company is served by an AML/CFT-reporting entity, beneficial owners controlling 25% or more of shares are identified and periodically re-verified under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book for Board and Shareholder Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - 850 per annum for professional registered office and corporate secretarial agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - 60,000 per engagement for a certified independent audit of an aviation engine leasing special purpose entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand offers a 15% R&D Tax Incentive credit on eligible R&D expenditure, immediate expensing for low-value assets, and industry-specific depreciation rates for aircraft engines and leasing assets. Companies may also benefit from imputation credits, which attach to dividends and reduce the overall tax burden for New Zealand-resident shareholders. No federal-state tax distinction applies as New Zealand is a unitary national jurisdiction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Tax Return filed electronically through the New Zealand Inland Revenue myIR secure online portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IR4 annual return is due by the 7th day of the month following the company's balance date. Companies with a tax agent and a standard 31 March balance date generally obtain an automatic extension to 30 June. Provisional tax payments are generally due in three instalments (8th month, 12th month, and 4th month after balance date) unless the company qualifies as a non-resident or small enterprise exempt from provisional tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income derived during the income year including all assessable New Zealand-sourced income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross rental and lease income from aircraft engine dry-leasing contracts where the lessee is New Zealand-resident or the asset is physically located in New Zealand; apply sourcing rules under section YD4 of the Income Tax Act 2007.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenses incurred in deriving the assessable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible expenses include engine depreciation, maintenance and overhaul reserves, financing costs (subject to thin capitalisation limitations), insurance, and administrative expenses. Non-resident lessors must apportion expenses that relate partly to non-New Zealand-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income before losses and allocation of imputation credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute net business income arising from the New Zealand leasing operation; ensure that any profit-shifting through intra-group fees or head office charges is adjusted to an arm's length basis.

Loss carryforward is subject to continuity of shareholding of at least 49% (same ultimate shareholders) under section IA 5; losses of a New Zealand branch of a non-resident may be ring-fenced and unusable against foreign income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual income tax (RIT) calculation after deducting RWT, foreign tax credits, and imputation credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident lessors without a New Zealand permanent establishment are generally subject to final non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on gross lease or interest payments rather than assessed residual income tax; where a PE exists, net assessment applies with treaty protection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credit account (ICA) balance and dividend allocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company entering the New Zealand imputation regime must maintain an ICA; dividends paid to non-resident shareholders attach imputation credits and are subject to NRWT of 30% unless a supplementary dividend mechanism or treaty reduction applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a late filing penalty of NZD 250 for non-furnishing of the IR4 (increasing to NZD 500 if more than 12 months late). A further 1% per day late payment penalty applies to unpaid tax (capped at 10% of the initial amount) plus an incremental penalty after 6 months. Interest under section 120 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 accrues at the prescribed rate on unpaid tax until satisfied.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, reduced to 15% under most double tax agreements (e.g., the US-NZ DTA) where the recipient holds at least 10% of the voting power; fully imputed dividends may also attract a 5% supplementary dividend top-up mechanism for treaty partners.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced NRWT or exemption, the non-resident recipient must obtain and lodge a certificate of residence (IR871 form issued by New Zealand Inland Revenue, or the foreign tax authority equivalent) with the New Zealand payer before the payment is made. The payer files the certificate and applies the treaty rate using form IR67F withholding declaration. For interest, an approved issuer levy (2%) may substitute for NRWT if the payer is an approved issuer and the interest is paid to a non-resident. The payer must retain all treaty documentation for audit purposes, and a non-resident must generally file a New Zealand return to claim refunds of excess NRWT where the correct treaty rate was not applied at source.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT rate for interest and royalties is 15% (30% if the royalty is sourced to New Zealand and paid to a non-resident under the old regime). Most modern DTAs reduce interest withholding to 10% or exempt arm's length interest where no permanent establishment exists; royalties are commonly reduced to 5% or 10% under treaty. Critically, dry-leasing payments for aircraft engines are generally characterised as commercial leasing income rather than royalties under New Zealand law (section YD4), so they are not subject to royalty withholding unless the payment is economically equivalent to a licence or the lease constitutes a finance lease that recharacterises payments into principal and interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand's transfer pricing rules (Part G of the Income Tax Act 2007, section GC13 and the Transfer Pricing Guidelines) require contemporaneous documentation where cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZD 10 million in aggregate annual value. For aviation leasing transactions, the threshold applies to lease payments, engine maintenance services, and interest on shareholder debt; failure to maintain such documentation carries a penalty of up to NZD 100,000.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate a codified ESR regime comparable to UAE or Cayman, but the general anti-avoidance rule (section BG 1) and the associated reconstruction rule (section GA 1) impose a substance requirement on cross-border structures. The OECD base erosion and profit shifting (BEPS) minimum standards are incorporated through domestic rules, including the requirement that New Zealand companies claiming treaty benefits or tax deductions for intra-group payments must demonstrate genuine commercial rationale, physical presence, and actual decision-making. Thin capitalisation rules limit non-resident debt funding to 60% of assets (or 110% of the worldwide group debt ratio) and restrict interest deductions where the group's New Zealand assets exceed worldwide debt proportions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting New Zealand-source dry-leasing income from an IR4 return, fabricating engine maintenance invoices, or transferring lease receivables to an offshore shell entity without economic substance to avoid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Prosecution under section 143A of the Tax Administration Act 1994; evasion penalty of 150% of the tax shortfall; criminal fine up to NZD 50,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable under section 149 for tax shortfalls where they knowingly participate in evasion; courts may impose civil restitution, travel bans, and management prohibition orders under the Companies Act 1993.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a New Zealand Ltd with no employees, premises, or decision-making activity while executing aircraft engine dry-lease contracts or holding engines as a bare title conduit for a foreign affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the general anti-avoidance rule (s BG 1) and recharacterisation of the transaction under s GA 1; complete disallowance of interest and expense deductions; shortfall penalty of up to 100% (or 150% for abusive tax avoidance) under s 141D.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who orchestrate a facade arrangement breach their statutory duties of care and diligence under s 135 of the Companies Act 1993 and may be ordered to pay equitable compensation; they may also be assessed as personally liable for the company's tax shortfall under s 149.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting aircraft engine lease payments through an escrow account without conducting customer due diligence, failing to file a suspicious transaction report with the New Zealand Financial Intelligence Unit, or transacting with a sanctioned airline or a person on the UN or NZ sanctions list.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 of up to NZD 2 million for a reporting entity (company) and up to NZD 200,000 for an individual; infringement notices of up to NZD 20,000 per breach may also be issued.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers of a reporting entity are individually liable for failures to comply with AML/CFT obligations; a conviction can result in imprisonment of up to 2 years under s 111 of the Act, in addition to personal fines and disqualification from managing companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting the dry-lease rate for a turbofan engine below or above arm's length to shift profits to a low-tax jurisdiction, failing to maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for related-party transactions exceeding NZD 10 million, or failing to align lease terms (e.g., maintenance reserves, return conditions) with third-party comparables.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment under s GC 13 recharacterising the lease income and disallowing excessive deductions; compensating interest under s 120; documentation penalty up to NZD 100,000; shortfall penalty of up to 40% for gross carelessness under s 141A and up to 100% for knowing tax avoidance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign incorrect returns with knowledge of the mispricing may be personally assessed for the resulting tax shortfall under s 149; recovery actions may compel personal restitution and debarment from directorship.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Financing the New Zealand dry-leasing subsidiary or branch with excessive shareholder debt so that interest deductions exceed the 60% debt-to-asset safe harbour or the worldwide group debt ratio, effectively stripping New Zealand profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of the excess interest expense under section FE 4-FE 18; recharacterisation of excessive loans as equity; shortfall penalty of up to 40% where the non-compliance is deliberate or careless; interest and late payment penalties accrue until the assessed shortfall is paid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for approving the debt structure who knowingly allow excessive interest deductions face personal liability for the company's shortfall, including civil recovery proceedings and a potential order for repayment of diverted company funds.
